Use case: style-transfer. Redesign the reference MCP sequence diagram as a distinctly editorial PHOTO CUT-PAPER COLLAGE while retaining all seven messages and accurate chronology. CHANGE column order to LEFT "MCP server", CENTER "Client" with subtitle "Agent app", RIGHT "LLM". LLM MUST BE ON THE FAR RIGHT.
Wide landscape 2:1 canvas, warm ivory #EFEAE0 paper, grayscale photographic cutouts with cream cut edges, muted teal #A3CFCB backing scraps, yellow #FFE234 labels, small vermilion #E5432F accents, tasteful sparse black halftone dots and paper grain, natural shallow contact shadows. This should look like a sophisticated independent technology magazine collage, not a standard vector flowchart. At the top of each column add one small recognizable photographic collage object: LEFT a grayscale server rack cutout on teal paper, CENTER a grayscale laptop cutout on ivory paper, RIGHT a grayscale microchip cutout on yellow paper. No robot or brain. Under each object a bold crisp label: "MCP server", "Client" (and "Agent app"), "LLM". Top objects should occupy only upper 25% so the communication labels stay large. No enclosing rectangles around objects, layered paper collage silhouettes instead.
Below the three labels, retain three thin vertical dashed lifelines. Seven straight horizontal arrows below, ordered top to bottom, labels on small cream paper strips with subtle hand-cut edges and LARGE clean Archivo-like black type:
1 CENTER Client to LEFT MCP server: "List tools", LEFT-pointing arrow.
2 LEFT MCP server to CENTER Client: "Tool definitions", RIGHT-pointing arrow.
3 CENTER Client to RIGHT LLM: "Tool definitions", RIGHT-pointing arrow.
4 RIGHT LLM to CENTER Client: "Tool name + inputs", LEFT-pointing vermilion arrow.
5 CENTER Client to LEFT MCP server: "Call tool", LEFT-pointing vermilion arrow.
6 LEFT MCP server to CENTER Client: "Result", RIGHT-pointing arrow.
7 CENTER Client to RIGHT LLM: "Result", RIGHT-pointing arrow.
Exactly these seven rows in exactly this sequence, no numbers printed. Each arrow spans ONLY its two adjacent endpoints. Never connect server directly to LLM. All arrowheads must clearly point to destination. Precise arrow lines despite tactile collage. Keep labels unobscured with generous line spacing. One small caption at bottom: "Tool definitions = name, purpose, inputs". No additional text, logos, watermark, frames, decorative arrows, or extra objects. Preserve scientific clarity while making the headers and labels unmistakably tactile editorial collage.
